what: About fifteen places read the request's environment directly (blaze's own knobs by name, the lent environment of scripts, record reads). There is no one accessor that notes which variable a step read, so `what did this build read of its environment` had to be assembled from four places (Noting::env, Reads::hash, process_env_reads, Session::env_read) plus a prefix rule for BLAZE_*; a new direct read of a variable that is not BLAZE_* and not in the walk set would be missed by the no-op lane.
cause: the environment travels as a plain Vec<(String, String)> on the config
whys: each step was keyed by its own reads one at a time
nothing made a read of the request's environment go through a noting type
class: an input read through many doors, with no single place that records the read
prevention: a `.clippy.toml` ban on reading `Invocation::env` outside one accessor that takes the reader's name and notes the variable (as `EnvReads::var` does); not built
workaround: `serve::job::read_unasked` compares every BLAZE_* variable and the whole walk set for every answer
